title: Ukraine and Russia's asymmetric war of attrition
subhead: Kyiv and Moscow have stepped up attacks on each other's infrastructure in recent weeks, aiming to weaken the opposing economy and undermine morale. Ukraine has paid a heavier price because it does not possess ballistic missiles and finds it increasingly difficult to intercept those targeting its territory.

title: China's Xi embarks on diplomatic marathon, from regimes hostile to the West to the White House
subhead: At the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit, held Monday and Tuesday in Kyrgyzstan, Chinese President Xi Jinping reaffirmed his opposition to American imperialism just weeks before his meeting with Donald Trump in Washington.

title: British PM Andy Burnham vows to end decades of decline and reverse privatization
subhead: In his first speech before Parliament on Tuesday, Burnham promised to restore 'hope' to his fellow citizens, but stopped short of announcing any specific measures. The budget, which will determine the government's policy direction, will be unveiled at the end of October.

title: British Museum director Nicholas Cullinan: 'The Bayeux Tapestry, in a non-nationalistic way, is clearly part of our national identity'
subhead: With just seven days to go before the exhibition opens, the director of the British Museum, Nicholas Cullinan, reflects on the extraordinary journey involved in the loan and transfer of this monumental work from France to England.

title: US sees rising opposition to Flock, a network of 120,000 vehicle-identifying cameras
subhead: Protests are mounting against Flock, a license plate detection system sold by a private company, which is widely seen as an intrusive threat to civil liberties. Over 60 cities have ended contracts with the company due to public pressure.

title: 'Even our ancestors do not remember a flood of this scale:' Nepal villagers face apocalypse frozen in mud
subhead: Warned in time, many residents of Devighat managed to evacuate their homes just minutes before the mudslide killed over 900 people in Nepal and China.
